constraints: ADR-001 D5 / ARCHITECTURE §2.1 anti-corruption layer: a raw provider DTO must NEVER reach the caller — `fetch()` returns `unknown`, `normalize()` MUST turn it into a canonical zod type before the Registry returns it (packages/core/src/adapters/types.ts:15-28). An arbitrary-rows tier is in direct tension with this rule and needs an explicit, documented carve-out, not a quiet `z.any()`.

Standing precedent set against Nansen's own MCP server (docs/architectures/system-architecture.md:610-614): the project REFUSED to proxy an official vendor MCP because 'several of its tools return markdown text, which is unusable for canonical zod normalization (D5), and proxying would bypass our own cache, budget and SSRF gate'. Any proposal to just mount Dune's hosted MCP (api.dune.com/mcp/v1) hits this same recorded decision and must be argued against it explicitly.

ARCHITECTURE §8 'factory, not singleton': every stateful piece (registry, coverage, account-state, singleflight, throttle bucket map) is constructed per-instance and injected; no module-level singletons. A Dune layer must follow the same factory shape (packages/core/src/adapters/nansen/index.ts:522-546 is the reference implementation).

R-25 per-adapter SSRF isolation: `hosts` is the allowlist for THAT adapter only, never a merged/global list (packages/core/src/adapters/types.ts:61-66; enforced hop-by-hop at packages/core/src/net/safe-fetch.ts:209). A Dune adapter gets exactly `['api.dune.com']` and cannot borrow anyone else's.

safe-fetch is https-only for the INITIAL url and every redirect hop, max 3 redirects, and strips Authorization/*api-key* headers on cross-host redirects (safe-fetch.ts:196-201, 226-241). No transport may bypass safeFetch.

R-37 fail-closed pricing: an unrecognized capability or a missing cost-table row must resolve to `Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY`, NEVER 0 (nansen/cost-of.ts:71, 96-99). Dune's stub currently violates the spirit of this with `costOf: () => ({credits: 0})` (dune/index.ts:28).

ROADMAP principle 1 'Free-first' (docs/onchain-analytics/ROADMAP.md:13) explicitly names 'Dune-free' (2500 cr/mo) as part of the FREE tier, and ROADMAP.md:99 lists 'Dune Query API (free 2,500cr/мес)' among the free adapters — so a Dune layer is chartered as free-tier-first, not as a second paid provider.

ROADMAP.md:241 — Dune SIM (sim.dune.com) is a recorded do-not-build: sunset 01.08.2026 (4 days from today, 2026-07-27). Only the Query/Execution API (api.dune.com) is in scope; the registered host already reflects this.

Owner decision 2026-07-26 (smart-money-flows.ts:23-29): closed chain enums were removed from tool schemas because ~8.7k tokens of schema were paid on EVERY request. Any new tool schema must stay token-cheap — a wide/verbose input schema for SQL parameters will be measured against this.
gaps: NO free-form/tabular result type exists anywhere. `grep -rn 'z.record|passthrough()|z.unknown()|z.any()' packages/core/src packages/mcp-server/src` returns ZERO hits; `packages/core/src/types/index.ts:4-13` exports exactly 9 closed canonical schemas (Chain, Token, Balance/Wallet, Pool, Ohlcv, Snapshot, SmartMoneyFlow, EntityLabel, TokenRiskScore) and every tool output is one of them or a `.strict()` object (17 `.strict()` occurrences across packages/mcp-server/src/tools/*.ts). There is no `QueryResult{columns[], rows[][], meta}` shape and no schema in the repo that can carry columns the engine did not know at compile time. This is THE blocking gap.

MCP registration forces an OBJECT output shape: `server.registerTool(..., { inputSchema: XSchema.shape, outputSchema: XSchema.shape }, ...)` (chain-tvl.ts:76-77) passes `.shape`, which only exists on a `z.object`. A tool cannot return a bare top-level array of rows; rows must be nested inside an object, and the output schema must still be a zod object whose shape is statically known.

NO async job/polling machinery. Dune's Query API is execute → poll status → fetch results (docs/onchain-analytics/provider-matrix.md:10), but `safeFetch` is strictly one-shot request/response with `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS = 15_000` per hop (safe-fetch.ts:32) and no adapter anywhere contains a poll loop, backoff, or job-state persistence (grep for setTimeout/poll/backoff across packages/core/src/adapters/*/index.ts finds only comments plus rate-limit.ts's own waiter). The `ProviderAdapter.fetch` contract (types.ts:26) is a single `Promise<unknown>` with no cancellation token and no way to return a job handle.

The registered dune rateLimit is actively hostile to a poll loop. `{capacity: 2, refillPerSec: 0.1}` (providers.config.ts:116) = 1 token per 10 s. The throttle's backlog math (rate-limit.ts:130-140) gives waits of 10s/20s/30s for the 3rd/4th/5th token, and the 6th exceeds `MAX_WAIT_MS = 30_000` (rate-limit.ts:32) and throws `RateLimitRejectedError`. A poll loop that shares the bucket dies after ~5 polls; a Dune execution routinely takes longer than that.

The 10 MB cap is not enforced on the response shape Dune actually returns. `assertResponseSizeWithinCap` (safe-fetch.ts:147-154) reads `Content-Length` and, when the header is ABSENT, `return`s early with no check at all — the module's own docstring at :34-38 admits this: 'a response with NO Content-Length header (e.g. chunked transfer-encoding) is not currently capped mid-stream'. A large JSON result set served chunked streams straight into `await response.json()` unbounded. When Content-Length IS present the comparison is strict `>` (:151), so exactly 10485760 bytes passes and 10485761 throws `SafeFetchResponseTooLargeError`. Either way the failure mode is bad: a hard throw that discards an already-PAID query result, or no limit at all. (Which branch real Dune traffic takes is UNVERIFIED — no DUNE_API_KEY in .env, so no live call was possible this run.)

Cache memory is bounded by ENTRY COUNT, not bytes. `LruHotLayer` uses `new LRUCache({ max: maxEntries })` with `DEFAULT_MAX_ENTRIES = 500` (lru.ts:8,28) and no `maxSize`/`sizeCalculation`. 500 canonical Token objects is trivial; 500 multi-megabyte SQL result tables is not. The persistent layer stores the whole result as a single `value_json TEXT` column (ddl.ts:60, sqlite-store.ts:198) with no size guard either.

`ProviderAdapter.costOf` is DEAD CODE at the registry level. `CapabilityRegistry.resolve()` (registry.ts:174-338) never calls `costOf` — grep confirms the only real consumer is nansen's own `fetch()` via its private gate (nansen/index.ts:573-581). So there is no generic pre-flight cost check; every provider must re-implement budget enforcement INSIDE its own `fetch()`. A Dune adapter inherits that duplication.

`_meta.budget` is hardcoded to a single provider. `budget-meta.ts:9` types `provider: 'nansen'` as a LITERAL and `:38` calls `getUsage('nansen', ...)`; the docstring at :5-7 states widening it to `string` was deliberately declined as speculative. A second credit-metered provider cannot report its spend through the existing `_meta.budget` channel without editing this type.

Dune's stub prices itself as free: `costOf: () => ({ credits: 0 })` (dune/index.ts:28). If a future generic budget path ever starts consulting `ProviderAdapter.costOf`, this silently declares a credit-metered vendor free — the exact inverse of the R-37 fail-closed rule the nansen path enforces (cost-of.ts:71).

The cache key cannot distinguish two different SQL queries unless the SQL (or a query id + params) is part of `args`. `deriveArgsHash(capability, args)` (args-hash.ts:44-47) hashes only the capability string and the normalized args object. That is workable, but it means the raw SQL text becomes part of a sha256 cache key and, via `canonicalize`, part of a JSON.stringify — and there is no length bound on it anywhere, unlike the deliberate `MAX_CHAIN_INPUT_LENGTH` truncation applied to chain input (chain/errors.ts:37-40).

No route/capability exists for anything query-shaped. The `routes` table (providers.config.ts:23-76) is 17 entity-shaped capabilities; `CapabilityDescriptor.id` is a free `string` (types.ts:10) so adding one is cheap, but every consumer downstream (TTL table, coverage matrix, tool output schema) assumes the capability maps to ONE fixed canonical entity.

Dune has no BACKLOG entry and no remaining consumer. `grep -i dune docs/BACKLOG.md docs/KNOWN_ISSUES.md` returns nothing, and docs/architectures/open-questions.md:100 records that `token.risk` went to Nansen so 'the exact token.holders query id / SQL has no consumer to be authored for'. The work is untracked, and the one capability the stub reserves is orphaned.

A chain the engine does not know — `UnknownChainError` (chain/errors.ts:23-50), raised BEFORE any network call or credit reservation (the docstring at :19-21 states this is deliberate: 'a mistyped chain name is the most common way an agent misses on a PAID route, and paying for a typo would make widening the chain set a way to spend money'). A capability that exists but not on the requested chain — `CapabilityNotCoveredOnChainError` (chain/errors.ts:87-137), deliberately NOT merged with `CapabilityUnavailableError` because the two demand opposite caller reactions (the table at :75-78: 'not here, and it will not be' vs 'could work — fix the key, or retry later'). A repeat of a request whose response the engine could not parse — negative cache. `NegativeCacheEntry` (registry.ts:52-56) records a DETERMINISTIC `normalize()` failure for `NEGATIVE_TTL_SECONDS = 60` (ttl.ts:83) and replays the refusal with zero network calls and zero credits, tagged '[cached negative]' (registry.ts:274). Only normalize failures are cached, never fetch failures (registry.ts:288-291).

Anything routed to `dash-platform`'s live gRPC transport — same stub mechanism as dune: `NotImplementedInM1Error` (adapters/not-implemented-error.ts:10-15) behind an unconditional `isAvailable() === {ok:false}`; its registration carries `hosts: []` (providers.config.ts:133), so even an accidental call would be SSRF-blocked.

gaps: **У оживления Dune нет владельца-фазы.** M1 сузил и перенёс в M2 (ROADMAP.md:83); M2 явно отказался и переисточил `token.risk` на Nansen (task-005-m2-alpha-paid.md:399–406); open-questions.md:100 фиксирует «has no consumer to be authored for»; TASK-006 внёс в out-of-scope (TASK.md:448, PLAN.md:272). M3–M6 (ROADMAP.md:165–224) Dune не упоминают. Любой Dune-слой сегодня — расширение скоупа, требующее ADR/решения владельца, а не исполнение существующего плана.

**`costOf()` возвращает фиксированную цену ДО вызова** (types.ts:25; nansen/cost-of.ts читает статическую таблицу `x-credit-cost` из закоммиченной спеки — ROADMAP.md:123). Цена исполнения Dune-запроса зависит от объёма просканированных данных и заранее неизвестна. Гейт `checkAndReserve` резервирует конкретное число кредитов в `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` — механики «зарезервировали неизвестно сколько» нет. Это тот же класс, что закрытый Q-3 («the 0-credit tier is structurally unrefusable by a credit-denominated gate», KNOWN_ISSUES.md:106), только хуже: не 0, а неизвестно.

**Budget-guard привязан к Nansen на трёх уровнях**: гейт живёт внутри `adapters/nansen/index.ts` `fetch()` (open-questions.md:124–129), `_meta.budget.provider` — литерал `'nansen'` (budget-meta.ts:9), а `PAID_PROVIDER_IDS` содержит `'dune'`, но «no logic reads this column» (sqlite-store.ts:42–48). Второй платный провайдер требует обобщения гейта либо его дублирования.

**Нет примитива асинхронного/долгого вызова.** Все адаптеры — один запрос/один ответ через `safeFetch`; Dune Query API это execute → poll status → results (provider-matrix.md:10). Ретраи и circuit breaker **намеренно отсутствуют** (ARCHITECTURE.md:164). Плюс `rateLimit: {capacity:2, refillPerSec:0.1}` (providers.config.ts:116) = один токен в 10 секунд — поллинг задохнётся на собственном лимитере.

**Недоверенный текст неизвестной формы.** Существующие ограничители — пофилдовые для ИЗВЕСТНОЙ схемы (normalize.ts:18/21/23: 200 строк, 64 элемента, 256 символов). Результат чужого SQL — таблица с произвольным набором колонок; канонического zod-типа под неё нет, а D5 (ADR:89) требует, чтобы «всё, что отдают tools и хранит кеш» было каноническим типом. Ни `MAX_VENDOR_COLUMNS`, ни обобщённого усечения таблицы в коде нет.

**Кэш-ключ от произвольного SQL.** `deriveArgsHash` хэширует нормализованные аргументы тула (security.md:52–58). Если SQL/query_id авторит модель, текст запроса становится аргументом: `.max()`-границы на него не определены нигде, и любая переформулировка даёт новый ключ → кэш перестаёт экономить кредиты именно там, где они дороже всего.

**Нет TTL-строки под «произвольный запрос».** ttl.ts:21 покрывает только `token.holders`; всё прочее молча падает в `DEFAULT_TTL_SECONDS = 300` (ttl.ts:61) — ровно та авария, которую adversarial cycle 1 поймал для платных capability (ttl.ts:34–40: «Letting the spend rate of the project's first paid provider be decided by that fallback is an accident, not a decision»).

**Нет колонки `vendors.dune` в реестре сетей.** `chainSupport` обязан быть предикатом над колонками реестра (types.ts:41–43); для nansen колонка заполнена задачей 006-9, для dune — нет. Без неё `chainSupport` может вернуться только к литералу, что нарушает standing constraint 4 и повторяет уже исправленный дефект L-10 (dune/index.ts:19–24).

**Живой eval бесплатного контура не может покрыть Dune по конструкции** — eval/README.md:35–37: «**Free providers only** … an eval that bills you every run gets turned off, and a monitor that is off is worse than no monitor.» Dune Query API кредитуемый ⇒ либо отдельный, редко запускаемый credit-eval, либо Dune остаётся без живого мониторинга payload-дрейфа — того самого класса `degraded`, который стоил проекту четырёх дней (README:16–18).

**`safeFetch` не держит cap на chunked-ответах** — BACKLOG.md:19 (R-47 carry-over) «a chunked/no-Content-Length response bypasses the `maxResponseBytes` cap entirely (needs a streaming byte-counter over `response.body`)»; open-questions.md:39–40 то же. Ответ `GET /execution/{id}/results` — как раз потенциально крупный и потоковый.

**`execution_id` из ответа вендора попадает в URL следующего запроса.** security.md:76–79 (правило R-56c) сформулировано намеренно шире хостов: «any path in which data from the network influences the allowlist is forbidden». Валидации формы `execution_id` перед подстановкой в путь в коде сегодня нет (адаптера нет вовсе) — это надо закладывать в дизайн, а не обнаруживать в ревью.

**Провенанс.** Живо-записанная Dune-фикстура и текст SQL-запроса обязаны попасть в `docs/provenance.json` (security.md:165–192), иначе молчаливая правка неотличима от «вендор поменял ответ». Файлы перечисляются явно, не по glob (security.md:190–192) — то есть это ручной шаг, который легко забыть.

**Транспорт n8n → движок не выбран (OQ-M3-1).** open-questions.md:57–83: три варианта, ни один не выбран, «**Settled by an ADR at M3 kickoff**». Если Dune-запрос долгий, его естественный запуск — расписание, а расписание живёт в n8n; значит дизайн Dune-слоя упирается в нерешённый OQ-M3-1.

**«Просто подключим официальный Dune MCP» заблокировано прецедентом** — system-architecture.md:609–616 (проксирование обходит наш кэш/бюджет/SSRF-гейт, markdown непригоден для канонизации). Плюс verification-corrections.md:9 фиксирует 26 тулов, а не 29 — счётчики хардкодить запрещено (ADR:243).
